stories.title: Find My Things: New teachable AI tool helps blind and low-vision people locate lost personal items
stories.synopsis: Microsoft researchers built a teachable AI tool that lets blind and low-vision people train it to help with their own daily lives. Find My Things helps users locate lost personal items. It's available to try for free in the Seeing AI app.

stories.title: AI Forecasts Unlock Aid for Farmers Before Floods Strike
stories.synopsis: Google's AI-based Flood Hub gives flood warnings five days in advance, including in river basins without streamflow gauges. A nonprofit trial pairs those warnings with unconditional cash, so farmers can prepare before the water arrives. Trials in Africa suggest farmers improve their livelihoods with early cash, and a planned 2026 trial in northern Bangladesh would cover over 100,000 families.

stories.title: AI gets more diagnoses right than generalist doctors in medical challenge
stories.synopsis: Microsoft researchers report an AI tool called DxO that outperformed individual generalist physicians at diagnosing complex medical cases, in a paper published in the journal Science. It made an accurate diagnosis 83.2% of the time on complex published cases and reached 80.3% accuracy on emergency department admission cases. The researchers are careful to note this doesn't mean it is better than doctors in real-world practice.
